text:
Priya (People Ops): Quick drop — rolled out a short set of "Clarity + Coach" prompts for OKR conversations this quarter. Aim: get aligned outcomes, a crisp self-review blurb, and a 5-min manager coaching moment. Link: https://redwood.example/okrs/clarity-coach :sparkles:
Alex L.: Love it. Can you paste a copy-paste self-review template that I can add to calendar invites?
Priya (People Ops): Yep — super short copy you can paste. Use this 3-line structure in the invite or the form:

```
Self-review (3 lines):
1) What I shipped / biggest outcome: <one sentence, quant metric if possible>
2) Measurable impact: <metric or user outcome + why it mattered>
3) Growth ask / support needed: <one specific ask from manager or team>
```

Priya (People Ops): Example filled in:
```
1) Launched streaming cache -> reduced median inference p99 from 220ms to 160ms.
2) Cut infra cost per 1M tokens by 12% while improving throughput for background jobs.
3) Ask: 2 days of Ops pairing to automate rollback hooks for model rollouts.
```
Maya R.: Nice examples. Any manager prompts? I want a script for the 1:1 to avoid wandering.
Priya (People Ops): Manager 6-min flow (micro-script):

```
0-1m: Quick hello + confirm the 3-line self-review (read back one line).
1-3m: Ask: "Which result surprised you?" then "Where did you need help?"
3-5m: Coach: one tactical suggestion + agree on one action this week.
5-6m: Close: confirm who does what and when; schedule quick follow-up check.
```
Priya (People Ops): Short phrasing cues you can paste:
- "The one metric I want to protect is..."
- "What stopped you from moving faster?"
- "If we could remove one barrier this week it would be..."

Jamal P.: Can we add OKR alignment checks for cross-team work? Those are always fuzzy.
Priya (People Ops): Yup — include this 2-line alignment probe in manager notes:
```
Alignment check:
1) Which outcome of this OKR depends on another team? (name owner)
2) What minimal commitment do we need from them this sprint? (calendar + deliverable)
```
Alex L.: Perfect. Any guidance on writing the objective statement itself?
Priya (People Ops): Keep objectives to 8 words max, action + customer + impact. Example: "Reduce inference latency for hosted API by 20%". Key tip: add the measurable intent in the key result lines, not buried in the objective.
Maya R.: Can you share a tiny rubric managers can use to rate progress in weekly syncs?
Priya (People Ops): Short rubric (green/amber/red) with one-sentence triggers you can paste into notes:
- Green: On track — key results are progressing and no major blockers.
- Amber: Risk — one dependency or resource gap is blocking >1 week of progress.
- Red: Off-track — metric trend moving opposite direction or dependency dropped.

Priya (People Ops): Finally, a template subject line for calendar invites: "Q2 Goal Check — <Name> / <Objective short> — 10m". Copyable example: "Q2 Goal Check — Alex L. / Reduce inference latency — 10m"
Jamal P.: Will push to my direct reports. Thanks — super usable. :thumbsup:
